title: Cross-SDK pagination & robust retry helpers for vectors + reranker ergonomics
creator: Jordan Kim
description:
Background:
We have functional embeddings and reranking endpoints across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, but ergonomics and API parity for common production patterns (pagination, batching, retries, and streaming composition) are inconsistent. Teams are implementing fragile client-side helpers with subtle differences in semantics and backoff behaviour, causing maintenance surface area and occasional flakiness in high-concurrency workloads.

Goal:
Deliver a small set of cross-SDK helper primitives that:
- Provide canonical pagination iterators for list-style endpoints (cursor-based and token-limited), with consistent semantics across languages.
- Provide batching utilities for embeddings that support max-batch-size and max-batch-bytes boundaries plus optional per-batch metadata (ids, dedupe).
- Introduce a retry policy helper that encapsulates idempotency rules, jittered exponential backoff, and circuit-breaker hints for non-idempotent rerank calls.
- Unify streaming ergonomics so streaming reranker/embeddings flows can be composed with minimal glue: async generators (Python), AsyncIterable helpers (TS), and channel-style helpers (Go).
- Include complete examples (Python/TS/Go) demonstrating a chunk->embed->rerank pipeline using the helpers.

Non-goal:
We will not change public endpoint signatures or introduce breaking changes to existing functions in this sprint. Migration helpers will be provided where necessary.

Acceptance criteria:
1) API parity: cross-language helpers exist with matching feature set and documented examples.
2) Unit + integration tests covering typical and edge cases (batch overflow, partial failures, retry exhaustion, streaming cancelation).
3) Benchmarks: helpers should not add more than 3-5% CPU overhead vs naive client loops; batching should reduce token cost by at least 10% in synthetic workloads.
4) Docs: new examples added to SDK readmes and a short migration guide in the Console docs.
5) Observability: SDK emits consistent telemetry tags for batch_id, retry_reason, and stream_session_id.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Batching boundaries: prefer a dual-threshold approach (item count + byte-size) to avoid oversized GPU batches. This is more complex but necessary for robust mem behaviour across models.
- Retry policy: default to safe behavior for rerank endpoints (which can be non-idempotent): 2 retries for non-critical rerank requests, 5 retries for embeddings (idempotent). Provide an opt-in aggressive mode for high-availability customers.
- Streaming composition: expose small utilities rather than heavy abstractions (e.g., combine_streams in Python as a generator wrapper). Heavy abstractions were rejected to keep SDK surface minimal and easy to debug.
- Backpressure: in TS/Go, provide optional backpressure hooks to let application code pause source iterator when downstream is saturated. In Python we use asyncio.Queue with a configurable maxsize.

API sketches (conceptual, not final signatures):
- Python:
  - EmbeddingBatcher(max_items=64, max_bytes=1_200_000) -> async context manager / async iterator that yields batches.
  - paginate(endpoint_call, page_size=100) -> async generator yielding items; supports stop_on_stale_cursor flag.
  - RetryPolicy(type="idempotent"|"safe", retries=3, backoff_base_ms=100, max_backoff_ms=5000) -> decorator / wrapper.
  - compose_streams(*gens, merge_strategy="interleave") -> async generator for streaming results.
- TypeScript:
  - createBatcher({maxItems, maxBytes}) -> AsyncIterable<Batch> + onFlush hook.
  - paginateCursor(client.listVectors, {limit}) -> AsyncIterable.
  - withRetry(policy, fn) -> Promise wrapper that exposes attempt metadata.
- Go:
  - NewBatcher(maxItems int, maxBytes int) -> chan Batch, Close() semantics.
  - CursorPager(ctx, client.ListVectors, opts) -> channel of items with ctx cancellation.
  - RetryWrap(ctx, fn, opts) -> error + attempts.

Telemetry and observability:
- Instrumentation: emit batch_id, batch_size, batch_bytes, retry_attempt, retry_reason, stream_session_id.
- Add integration test that verifies metrics pipeline (mock telemetry returns expected tags).

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for boundary conditions in each SDK.
- Cross-SDK interop smoke test: a small Python producer that emits embeddings consumed by TS/Go reranker clients via helper-generated batches (run in CI matrix).
- Load test: synthetic workload of 200 concurrent clients, average batch size 24, validate that retry behaviour stays within SLOs.

Migration notes:
- Provide deprecation shims for current helper functions for one minor release.
- Include a migration example (one-liner) in the changelog.

Risks:
- Incorrect batch byte estimates leading to OOM on some models; mitigate with safe defaults and per-model overrides.
- SDK parity drift; include a small schema-driven test that asserts helper API shape across languages (script in repo).

2026-02-28 Miguel Alvarez (review): Left design feedback on the TS API—prefer AsyncIterable factory over returning an event emitter. Also suggested exposing attempt metadata to callers for observability. Added suggested small patch in PR review.
2026-03-01 Design review (Nina Park): Approve streaming ergonomics for Python/TS. Ask for a short example UI snippet showing how Console can visualize stream_session_id telemetry.

2026-03-02 Asha Patel: Go helper prototype completed (pkg/helpers/batcher). Running CI matrix: go, python, ts. Found race when closing channel under cancellation; fixed by adding CloseWait semantics. Benchmark results attached to PR show ~12% reduction in token requests for batched embeddings on synthetic dataset.
